clue.text: Competent books on orally transmitted infection

indicators.note: in a down clue, books placed on the first piece sit underneath it, so they come after
transmitted orally means passed on by mouth, i.e. spoken, so the word for the infection is said rather than spelt

parts.note: flu is a common viral infection, and it is spread through the air by coughs
NT is the New Testament, the later books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A doctor's verdict that someone is skilled at books about an infection passed on by mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orally transmitted' is the sound signal: the infection said aloud gives FLUE, a chimney pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fluent in a skill or language is able and capable, so it is a synonym for competent.

clue.text: Close friend is badly late for The King and I

indicators.note: badly suggests the word late has gone wrong, its letters scrambled

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king
ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: A friend arrives too late for a performance of the musical The King and I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King and I' looks like the title of the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical, but it is wordplay: Rex for the king and the Latin pronoun for I.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego is a second self, hence a trusted bosom friend in older usage.

clue.text: Confined to the pub

definitions.meaning: restricted to one area, as in a problem limited to one district
a Briton's nearest regular public house, where they usually drink

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both limited to a neighbourhood and, in British slang, one's neighbourhood public house.

clue.text: Would foremost stallions train under duress here?

definitions.text: Would foremost stallions train under duress here?

indicators.note: foremost asks for the leading letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A question about whether horses on a breeding farm are forced to train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foremost' takes the first letters of 'stallions train under duress'; the whole clue then describes the place, so it is an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a farm where stallions are kept for breeding, so stallions live there.

clue.text: People again soldier on, taking officer to east Iceland first

indicators.note: first says the Iceland piece comes before the east piece
taking means the first pair of words holds the officer within them

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps, standing for a soldier
COL is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer
IS is the international vehicle code for Iceland
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Military orders to carry on, with an officer heading out to eastern Iceland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'People' is a verb here, to populate.
explanation.definitionFit: To recolonise a land is to settle and populate it once more, so it means to people again.

clue.text: Question for motoring organisation about water

indicators.note: about means the motoring body's letters surround the question

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British breakdown and motoring club

explanation.surface: Someone asks the breakdown club a query about water.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua is the Latin word for water, used in English compounds and labels.

clue.text: A sign that 11 is in India

parts.note: the answer to 11 across is a green precious stone, so a gem
taken as written
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A star sign that a green stone is in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' and 'is' are links; the cross-reference is to 11 across, whose answer is a gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: This month, a northern church, for example

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means of the current month in old business letters
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A diary note about this month, a northern church, given as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; 'inst.' is old commercial shorthand for this month.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case cited to illustrate something, so it is a synonym for example.

clue.text: Flower girl from the glen

parts.note: a girl's first name that is also a flower name
of means from, as in a man of Kent
a glen is a narrow Scottish dale between hills

explanation.surface: A flower girl who comes from a Scottish glen.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant with tiny white bells is a well-known spring flower, and in the setter's May theme it blooms in May.

clue.text: She commands state to cede southern territory

indicators.note: to cede is to give up, so the state gives away those letters

parts.note: Queensland is a state of Australia
land is territory

explanation.surface: A ruler orders a state to give up territory in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: A reigning monarch who is female gives orders, so she is a woman in command.

clue.text: Dear me! Linda's starting to turn green!

indicators.note: to turn means the letters change round into a new order
starting takes the opening letter of Linda's

explanation.surface: An alarmed exclamation as Linda starts turning green.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald is a vivid shade of green, named after the gemstone.

clue.text: Tailors working for deaf teacher

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being worked into another shape

explanation.surface: Tailors at work for a teacher who is deaf.
explanation.definitionFit: An oralist teaches deaf people by lip-reading and speech rather than sign language.

clue.text: May be a heartless trainee

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letters of the word trainee

explanation.surface: A suggestion that someone may be a trainee lacking compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the verb but is the hawthorn, called the May tree; 'be a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: May is another name for hawthorn, which blossoms in that month.

clue.text: Contest the aspiration of the Maastricht Treaty?

definitions.meaning: the annual European song competition televised across the continent

definitions.text: the aspiration of the Maastricht Treaty?
definitions.meaning: the treaty that founded the European Union had a vision of Europe, split into two words

explanation.definitionFit: The song contest's name, taken apart, reads as a European aim, fitting the treaty that made the EU.

clue.text: Released a French degenerate before coming to a sticky end

indicators.note: before places the previous pieces ahead of the last one

parts.note: un is the French for a
loose means dissolute or immoral, like a degenerate

indicators.note: sticky suggests the word end comes out messed up

explanation.surface: A French degenerate is let go before meeting an unpleasant fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to a' is a link; 'sticky' scrambles END into NED.
explanation.definitionFit: To unloose something is to set it free, so the past form means released.

clue.text: What's outstanding when contents become contentious?

indicators.note: contents become contentious when extra letters are put in, so those letters are what is left of the longer word once contents is taken away

parts.note: the longer word, from which the shorter one is taken away; that the leftover letters sit together inside it is a coincidence of the deletion, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: A question about what remains unresolved when the contents of something cause a row.
explanation.walkthrough: Insert these letters into CONTENTS and it becomes CONTENTIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt, money still outstanding.

clue.text: Strength of evidence

definitions.meaning: the alcoholic strength of a spirit, measured on a scale
facts that establish the truth of something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the alcohol content of a spirit and conclusive evidence.

clue.text: Musical instrument sounds like a parrot's call — almost!

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is not used
sounds like means the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Polly is the traditional name for a pet parrot; to phone is to make a call

explanation.surface: A musical instrument that sounds nearly like a parrot squawking.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'Polly phone' gives POLYPHONE; 'almost' drops the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyphon is a large Victorian music box playing tunes from metal discs.

clue.text: Hurry, knowing about trap

explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link. A trap and a fly were both light one-horse carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to dash, is slang for streetwise, and names a light horse-drawn carriage like a trap.

clue.text: Even in Almeria there is floral decoration

indicators.note: even asks for the letters in the even positions, second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Flowers even in the Spanish town of Almeria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'there is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn round the neck.

clue.text: Relative is muddled, leaving Arkansas behind

indicators.note: leaving means those letters depart and go behind, off the end

parts.note: unclear means confused or muddled
AR is the postal abbreviation for Arkansas

explanation.surface: A relative is confused about leaving Arkansas behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' and 'behind' are links; AR comes off the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a family member, a relative.

clue.text: Is part of goal to frustrate counsel?

parts.note: to cross someone is to thwart or frustrate them
the Bar is the body of barristers, legal counsel

explanation.surface: Is it a goal to thwart the lawyer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossbar is the horizontal top beam of football goalposts.

clue.text: Romantic actor heard he'd got the bird on May 3rd!

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: luvvie is British slang for a gushing actor
a dove is a bird of the pigeon family

indicators.note: 3rd takes the third letter of May

explanation.surface: An actor got the bird, booed off stage, on the third of May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he'd got the' and 'on' are links; to 'get the bird' is to be booed, but here the bird is a DOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes sentimental, openly affectionate behaviour, a romantic mood.

clue.text: See 9
Limit of support

definitions.meaning: an extreme point, like the north or south end of the earth
a post or staff holding something up

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an extreme point of the globe and a post that holds things up.

clue.text: Hesitate before admitting one owns fur!

indicators.note: before puts the hesitation ahead of the next piece

parts.note: er is the sound of someone hesitating
a person who says it belongs to them uses this possessive

explanation.surface: A hesitant confession that a fur coat belongs to the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat, used on royal robes.

clue.text: Short's got nothing in enclosure

indicators.note: in means the nothing goes inside the word for short

parts.note: curt means short or brusque
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A short person has got nothing inside a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A court is a courtyard, an area enclosed by walls or buildings.

clue.text: Web-footed friend joins struggling team

parts.note: pal is an informal word for friend

indicators.note: struggling suggests the team is in disarray, its letters in a mess

explanation.surface: A friend joins a team that is struggling, with a duck-footed twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmate describes webbed feet, like a hand-shaped leaf.

clue.text: Heartless beast is a bit solitary too

indicators.note: heartless removes the inside letters of the word for beast, leaving its ends

parts.note: an animal is a beast

indicators.note: a bit takes just the opening part of the word solitary, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A cruel creature is also rather a loner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; 'a bit' supplies SO, the first two letters of 'solitary'.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too both mean in addition, interchangeable adverbs.

clue.text: Mature crowd return to accept defeat

indicators.note: to accept means the reversed crowd takes the defeat inside it
return means the word for crowd is read backwards

parts.note: a mob is a crowd
a loss is a defeat

explanation.surface: A grown-up crowd goes back to admit losing.
explanation.definitionFit: To blossom is to develop or come to maturity, so it means to mature.

clue.text: Gamble on getting best mark in second grade

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the mark, so before it

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
A is the top grade in marking

explanation.surface: A gamble on getting top marks in a second-grade exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, used for a second-class grade.

clue.text: Wherein he now ensured gold medal status

definitions.text: Wherein he now ensured gold medal status

indicators.note: wherein means the name lies inside the following words

explanation.surface: Describing the moment an athlete secured his Olympic gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across 'nOW ENSured'; the whole clue also describes Jesse Owens, the US sprinter who won four golds in 1936.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesse Owens won four Olympic gold medals at Berlin, so his place is assured.

clue.text: Is the internet a means to divert?

indicators.note: means to suggests the letters are a way of making the answer, rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether the internet is a way to amuse oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain people is to amuse them, to divert them.
